newsitem.title: GERMANY: German state NRW says May CPI up 0.4 pct mth/mth.
newsitem.headline: German state NRW says May CPI up 0.4 pct mth/mth.

text.p: The statistics Office in the west German state of North Rhine-Westphalia said on Monday the cost of living rose 0.4 percent month-on-month in May for an annual rate of 1.8 percent.
The state said consumer prices fell 0.1 percent month-on-month in April for an annual rate of 1.6 percent.
North Rhine-Westphalia is one of four west German states whose consumer price reports are used to compute provisional west German consumer prices.
The other three states -- Bavaria, Baden-Wuerttemberg and Hesse -- have all reported consumer price data for May. The figures were generally above analysts' market expectations.

Bavaria said consumer prices rose 0.5 percent from April and 1.5 percent year-on-year. Baden-Wuerttemberg reported that consumer prices for May rose 0.3 percent over April for an annual rate of 1.3 percent.
Hesse said consumer prices in May rose 0.3 percent from April and 1.2 percent year-on-year.
German state NRW says May CPI up 0.4 pct mth/mth

The state office noted the rise was due in part to seasonal factors, such as an 8.1 percent month-on-month rise in the cost for package holidays and higher prices for foodstuffs, including coffee and potatoes.
